text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co said on Friday that it is voluntarily recalling an individual lot of 150,000 compact units of the oral contraceptive Ovcon 35 from markets in the United States and its territories.
The company said it has received several reports of mispackaged product in which color-coded tablets are in reverse order of the package design.

According to Bristol-Myers, there is no significant health threat posed to women who may already have taken the incorrect tablets, and it is highly unlikely that pregnancy would occur as a result of taking the mispackaged placebo tablets instead of the tablets with active ingredient.
It is possible, however, that some women could experience irregularity in their menstrual cycle, which should correct itself when the normal dosing regimen is resumed, Bristol-Myers said.

A company spokesman told Reuters that the financial impact of the recall would be minimal. He said that combined annual sales of Ovcom 35 and Ovcom 50, a stronger dosage that is not affected by the recall, is $40 million.
The U.S. Food & Drug Administration has been notified of this recall, the company said.
